deepDive.title: Speed-time graphs — reading motion like a scientist
deepDive.body: Class 7 uses distance-time graphs. Class 8 introduces SPEED-TIME graphs — a more powerful tool. On a speed-time graph: x = time, y = speed. A FLAT horizontal line = constant speed (uniform motion). UPWARD slope = ACCELERATING (speed increasing). DOWNWARD slope = decelerating. The AREA UNDER THE LINE = distance travelled. So a cyclist at 15 km/h for 2 hours: rectangular area = 15 × 2 = 30 km distance. A train accelerating from 0 to 100 km/h over 1 hour: triangular area = ½ × 1 × 100 = 50 km. This is a tiny piece of integral calculus — areas under curves give totals. Vande Bharat's progress can be visualised as one zig-zag speed-time graph; engineers analyse it to find efficient speed profiles.
deepDive.nextStepHint: Class 9 introduces acceleration formula and three equations of motion.

deepDive.title: Three equations of motion — predicting where things end up
deepDive.body: Class 7 has v = d/t (speed = distance / time). Class 9 introduces THREE equations of motion for objects with constant acceleration: (1) v = u + at — final velocity from initial velocity, acceleration, time. (2) s = ut + ½at² — distance covered. (3) v² = u² + 2as — final velocity given distance covered. Where u = initial velocity, v = final, a = acceleration, t = time, s = distance. Practical: a sprinter accelerating at 5 m/s² from rest, after 2 seconds: v = 0 + 5 × 2 = 10 m/s. Distance: s = 0 + ½ × 5 × 4 = 10 m. These three equations predict every projectile, falling ball, accelerating car. Every JEE problem on motion uses these three. Indian Olympic sprinters' training is partly based on these equations + biomechanics.
deepDive.nextStepHint: Class 11 extends to 2D motion (projectile, circular) with vector equations of motion.

deepDive.title: Pendulum SHM — the math of swing time
deepDive.body: Class 7 says pendulum period depends on length. Class 11 gives the formula: T = 2π√(L/g), where T = time period, L = length, g = gravity (9.8 m/s² on Earth). So 1m pendulum: T = 2π√(1/9.8) ≈ 2.0 seconds. Half the length: T = 2π√(0.5/9.8) ≈ 1.4 sec — NOT half, but √2 less. Quadrupling length doubles the period. Why depends on g? On the Moon (g = 1.6), same pendulum: T ≈ 5 sec — Moon clocks would tick slowly. SIMPLE HARMONIC MOTION (SHM): pendulum's swing pattern repeats sinusoidally. Same math describes vibrating springs, sound waves, AC current alternation. Even Indian classical music's tabla bols are described by SHM frequencies.
deepDive.nextStepHint: JEE tests SHM amplitude, frequency, phase + the energy oscillation between potential and kinetic.
